title: Hiring SLAs & Time-to-Offer Operational Runbook
content:
Purpose:
This runbook defines target SLAs across the core hiring stages and prescriptive ops steps to meet a 14-day median time-to-offer for non-executive roles. It's intended for recruiting coordinators, hiring managers, and People Ops on-call. Treat as living: updates logged to CONFLUENCE-3245.

Context / why this matters: 
- Time-to-offer correlates with candidate experience and offer acceptance, and is a leading indicator for hiring velocity.
- We have spikes in some teams (infra, SRE) that push up median; a standardized SLA model reduces ad-hoc exceptions.

Target SLAs (operational targets, not absolute guarantees):
- Requisition approval (Req -> live): 48 hours (team PR approves + hiring manager sign-off).
- First sourcer outreach -> first phone screen scheduled: 72 hours.
- Phone screen -> onsites scheduled (core loop): 7 calendar days.
- Onsite loop completed -> hiring committee decision: 48 hours.
- Decision -> written offer extended: 24 hours.
- Offer -> acceptance target: 7 calendar days (longer for international/relocation).
- Total median time-to-offer (req open -> offer): 14 calendar days (target for 70th percentile non-exec roles).

Operational flows (owner responsibilities & checklists):
1) Requisition kickoff (recruiter + HM) — owner: recruiter
- Checklist: job brief in ATS, hiring rubric sketched, core interviewers named, calendar blackout windows flagged, salary band confirmed.
- If req not approved in 48 hrs escalate to People Ops lead (Slack: @aisha).

2) Sourcing cadence — owner: sourcer
- Days 0–3: 25 outbound touches minimum (LinkedIn, referrals).
- Track reach rate in ATS pipeline column "reach-rate".
- If no engaged candidates by day 4, expand sourcing channels and request 1 cross-team referral.

3) Screening -> interview loop design — owner: recruiter + HM
- Phone screen completed within 7 days of first outreach. Phone screen template versioned in Confluence (see CONFLUENCE-3245).
- Interview loop should be compact: ideally 3–4 interviews in one-day or two half-days. Avoid >6 separate slots.
- Shared calendar blocks reserved for interview loops: coord to propose 3 candidate-friendly times within 48 hours of phone screen completion.

4) Decision & offer execution — owner: recruiter + People Ops (comp admin)
- Hiring committee meeting scheduled within 48 hrs of last interview. Committee note taker files Decision Note as a single paragraph summary (strengths/risks, recommend hire? yes/no).
- Recruiter prepares offer packet draft while committee meets.
- Offer must be routed to Comp Admin for band check same day. If comp approval not done within 8 hours, escalate to People Ops lead.

5) Candidate follow-through & background checks — owner: recruiter
- Offer letter sent within 24 hrs of decision (PDF + email template). Background check instructions included.
- For time-sensitive roles, send a heads-up card (short email) the same day as the decision to the hiring manager and candidate with next steps timeline.

Quick templates (use verbatim or adapt):
- Interview scheduling (email snippet): 
  "Thanks for your time — would any of these windows work for a 60–90m interview block? [options]. We'll send calendar invites and prep details once you confirm. Thanks! — [Recruiter name]"
- Offer extension (subject): "Redwood: Offer for [Role]"
  Body (first para): "We're excited to offer you the role of [Role]. This email summarizes compensation and next steps; a formal PDF offer is attached. Please review and tell us any questions by [date 72 hours]. If you need more time, let us know and we'll do our best to accommodate."

Escalation matrix (fast-path triggers):
- If candidate cancels 2 scheduled interviews -> recruiter to check in; if reschedule pushes decision beyond target SLA, mark as "time-sensitive" and escalate to People Ops.
- If any step slips >48 hrs beyond SLA: auto-notify slack #recruiting-ops with tag @people-ops.
- Comp approval pending >8 hours -> escalate to People Ops lead.

Exception handling & allowed deviations:
- Senior / Exec roles: SLAs are advisory; time-to-offer target: 30–45 days.
- Relocation & work-authorization roles: add +7–14 days for immigration/sponsorship checks.
- Candidate-requested timeline extensions should be recorded in ATS and treated as "candidate delay" not an ops slip.

Metrics & dashboards (what we track):
- Median time-to-offer (req open -> offer sent).
- Stage-level medians (sourcing->screen; screen->loop; loop->decision; decision->offer).
- Offer acceptance rate by band & team.
- Candidate NPS excerpt (post-process survey).
- Dashboards: dashboard://hiring-ops/time-to-offer and Looker report HiringOps_TTO_v2.

On-call playbook (when SLAs break):
- During a 2-week hiring surge, activate "rapid response": recruiting lead assigns a coordinator, sourcer floats between teams, and daily 09:15 standup to hit 14-day target.
- Use "rapid-response" tag in ATS to prioritize scheduling.

Runbook do/don't & best practices (notes from pilot runs):
- DO batch onsite windows so interviewers can clear schedules and give quicker decisions.
- DO provide interview prep notes to candidates (what to expect).
- DON'T schedule single-interviewer slot loops spread across more than 7 days.
- DO include salary band in req to avoid comp delays.

Operational tasks for the next 30 days (owner assignments):
- Recruiters: enforce 72-hr outreach -> identify 10 reqs currently exceeding SLA and create remediation plans.
- People Ops: add "time-to-offer" column to weekly hiring snapshot and present to GTM/Eng leads.
- Engineering managers: commit to 2 interview-day windows/week to improve scheduling density.

Open questions / unresolved items (placeholders to iterate on in CONFLUENCE-3245):
- Finalize whether on-call People Ops can approve comp overrides up to $5k without exec sign-off.
- Decide on language for candidate extensions greater than 7 days (standard response).

Notes and audit trail: 
- Pilot run (Q3 2025) reduced median TTO from 21 -> 15 days for non-exec roles when teams committed to 2 interview days/week.
- Keep raw logs for 12 months in ATS export for retrospective analysis (see JIRA-HIRE-1123 archive).

Contact & ownership: 
- Runbook owner: Aisha Patel (people-ops) — Slack @aisha, pager for escalations.
- Backup owner: Liam Chen.

Revision log: 
- 2025-10-28 created (baseline SLA draft)
- 2025-11-15 updated: shortened phone-screen -> loop SLA from 10 -> 7 days; added comp-approval escalation window.

Quick checklist (copyable to interview coordinator templates):
- [ ] Req signed & banded (48h)
- [ ] 25 outbound touches (days 0–3)
- [ ] Phone screen scheduled within 72h of outreach
- [ ] Loop windows proposed within 48h of phone screen
- [ ] Committee decision recorded within 48h of loop completion
- [ ] Offer sent within 24h of decision

End of runbook — keep feedback in CONFLUENCE-3245 or ping @aisha for urgent SLA exceptions.
